name: Spoofing and lie detection (signals)
plain: Checks whether language, resolution, OS or browser values were faked and whether an ad blocker is on.
meaning: Compares claimed values with probed ones to spot people using privacy tools or anti-detect browsers. The result becomes a fingerprint signal in itself.

web.api: Fingerprint2.js style checks: liedLanguages, liedResolution, liedOS, liedBrowser, adBlockInstalled

steps: Compare screen sizes with available sizes
Compare UA OS with platform and touch
Compare UA browser with feature probes
Probe for ad blocker bait elements

limits.headline: Can check whether your browser settings were faked or an ad blocker is on
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Compare your claimed language, screen size and system with what the browser actually shows
Tell if an ad blocker is running

See your name or account by itself
Be stopped by a browser pop up, since none exists

story.what_it_is: A script checks whether your browser's reported language, screen or system were faked, and whether an ad blocker is on.
story.for_you: You never see it. The site quietly checks that the story your browser tells is consistent. If it looks faked, you may get an extra check, a CAPTCHA, or a blocked checkout with no clear reason.
story.for_makers: Fraud and bot teams use it to catch people who hide behind fake settings. Ad networks use it to spot ad blockers and bots. It also lets trackers notice who is trying to avoid them.

use_cases.example: A fraud tool sees a browser claiming to be an iPhone but acting like a Linux server, and flags it as a bot.
Fraud checks compare your reported time zone, language and device. A mismatch can send an order for manual review.
An ad network tests for fake traffic. If the browser lies about its screen size, the click is not billed to the advertiser.
A free to play browser game bans players who fake their device to farm rewards many times.
A news site detects an ad blocker and shows a polite wall asking you to turn it off or subscribe.
A ticket site spots scalper bots that fake many different devices to grab seats, and lets real fans through.
Analytics tools filter out visits where values were spoofed, so charts are not full of fake visitors.

risks: Can single out people who hide

technical_bounds: Cannot tell which tool caused the mismatch
